newsitem.title: USA: GM pushing parts suppliers on costs - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: GM pushing parts suppliers on costs - WSJ.

text.p: General Motors Corp is about to tell its parts suppliers around the world that they must hold down warranty-repair costs or risk paying penalties, the Wall Street Journal said.

In Friday's electronic edition, the Journal said that Harold Kutner, GM's vice president in charge of international purchasing, plans to make the initiative a major focus during an address to suppliers this weekend in Rio de Janeiro.

The requirements are designed to put a greater focus on quality among GM's $70 billion annual parts purchases. The requirements are to be part of any purchasing contracts the auto maker signs with a supplier, Kutner told the Journal.

"That warranty number will become part of the commitment, like cost and price," Kutner said. "Our process is based on competition. The suppliers will tell us what they can do with quality, and that target will become part of the contract."

The push is part of a trend in the world auto-parts industry. GM and other auto makers are demanding that leading suppliers take on more responsibility for design and development of the parts they make, as well as to push costs down while improving quality.
